5. Supervised Versus Unsupervised Pretraining
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446294294-603796229.png
This connects back to labeled input-output pairs, already covered in this topic. Pretraining, already covered generally in Transfer Learning, genuinely learns from raw, unlabeled text.
SFT genuinely instead requires genuinely labeled, curated examples with genuinely known correct answers, a genuinely fundamental contrast explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This contrast, already covered in this topic, directly explains why SFT datasets are genuinely far smaller than pretraining corpora, already covered generally in Transfer Learning: creating labeled examples genuinely requires real human effort.

10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates a small labeled dataset, already covered in this topic, used for supervised fine-tuning.

code.content:
# already covered as labeled input output pairs in this topic
sft_dataset = [
    {"input": "What is the capital of France?", "output": "The capital of France is Paris."},
    {"input": "Explain photosynthesis briefly.", "output": "Photosynthesis is how plants convert sunlight into energy."},
    {"input": "What is 12 times 7?", "output": "12 times 7 is 84."},
]

def training_pair(example):
    # already covered as labeled input output pairs in this topic
    return {"prompt": example["input"], "target": example["output"]}

print("SFT training pairs (already covered in this topic):\n")
for example in sft_dataset:
    pair = training_pair(example)
    print(f"Prompt: {pair['prompt']}")
    print(f"Target: {pair['target']}")
    print("---")

# already covered as dataset quality mattering most here in this topic
print(f"\nDataset size (already covered as dataset quality mattering most in this topic): {len(sft_dataset)} carefully labeled examples")

blocks.content: Running this example shows a small handful of carefully labeled input-output pairs, exactly the kind of curated data already covered in this topic that SFT depends on, rather than raw, unlabeled text.

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Supervised Fine-Tuning trains on labeled input-output pairs with a known correct answer.
Instruction tuning is one specific example of this broader supervised fine-tuning category.
Every SFT example has an input paired with one known, human-approved correct output.
Pretraining learns from raw, unlabeled text; SFT requires labeled, curated examples instead.
Because every example carries an explicit label, dataset quality matters enormously for SFT.
A small, high-quality SFT dataset often outperforms a large, noisy one.
SFT bridges a purely predictive pretrained model toward following human intent, though not fully aligned.
Real pipelines typically run SFT before RLHF, getting the model roughly right before further refinement.
Next up: RLHF, refining an already SFT-trained model further using explicit human feedback.
